summary: The new template engine lazily evaluates nested and recursive templates only when accessed and caches intermediate results within an operation, giving large performance gains for complex templating.
questions: Does Ansible evaluate nested variables lazily now?
Why were deeply nested templates slow in older Ansible?

answer_card.title: Lazy templating improves performance
answer_card.answer_md: Older versions resolved deeply nested, recursive or self-referential templates to full depth on every access, even for data that was never used. The new engine **defers templating until values are accessed** (or leave the engine) and **caches** intermediate results for the duration of a template operation. This has produced exponential speedups in many real-world complex templating cases.
